title: Intermediate Backend Engineer , Security Factory
description: div class= content-intro p GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. /p p The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values nbsp;and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. a href= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI Co-create the future with us /a as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. /p p * em Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. /em /p /div h2 strong An overview of this role /strong /h2 p As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them. /p p Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities. /p p We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role. /p h2 strong What you'll do /strong /h2 ul li Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks. /li li Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates. /li li Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work. /li li Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync. /li li Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review. /li li Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down. /li li Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review. /li li Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues. /li /ul h2 strong What you'll bring /strong /h2 ul li Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy. /li li Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them. /li li An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it. /li li Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment. /li li The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions. /li li Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome. /li /ul h2 strong About the team /strong /h2 p The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones. /p p At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world

title: Analyst, Risk Management
description: div class= content-intro p Razorpay is one of India’s leading full-stack financial technology companies, powering the way businesses move, manage, and grow money. Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar with a simple vision - to simplify payments for Indian businesses - we’ve since grown into a fintech powerhouse driving India’s digital payment revolution. /p p Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow. /p p From building AI-native agentic payments, to AI-assisted fraud detection and real-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners - including banks, networks, regulators - we are pioneering industry-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech /p p Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation - powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia. /p p Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently. /p p Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme - and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region. /p p We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India amp; SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions - including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards-first UPI) - along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia. /p p But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen - you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle - if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People gt; Pedigree - we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles - this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy amp; Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors, nbsp; you’ll be part of a 3000+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future. /p /div p strong The Role: nbsp; /strong /p p The role will involve establishing and nurturing relationships with channel partners to promote and sell our products or services. You will play a critical role in expanding our business through strategic partnerships and ensuring the successful onboarding of new partners. nbsp; /p p strong Job Summary nbsp; /strong /p p This role requires strong knowledge and experience in Sanctions, AML (Anti-Money Laundering), and Financial Crimes. The position will focus on Customer Due Diligence (CDD), website assessment, risk assessment associated with merchant onboarding, and Transaction Monitoring, covering all aspects of business model validation and compliance. nbsp; /p p strong Roles and Responsibilities nbsp; /strong /p ul li Conduct onboarding and ongoing customer due diligence. nbsp; /li li Conduct and perform quality control relative to a variety of investigation types, including suspicious activity, sanctions, and enhanced due diligence (EDD). nbsp; /li li Manage daily escalation queues, handling complex or exception cases from business and operations teams. nbsp; /li li Participate in process improvement, identifying and implementing best practices in effective and innovative ways. nbsp; /li li Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) with comprehensive knowledge about AML policies, fraud control, risk categorization policies, monitoring, evaluation, review, and associated reporting. nbsp; /li li Demonstrate excellent knowledge of reporting procedures and record-keeping guidelines. nbsp; /li li Maintain the ability to communicate clearly and precisely to the point with stakeholders. ● Should be familiar with essential screening tools, including Dow Jones and LexisNexis. nbsp; /li /ul p strong Qualifications Required nbsp; /strong /p ul li Knowledge about a customer support application or CRM, such as Freshdesk. ○ Familiarity with Stages/levels of chargebacks, penalty involved at the arbitration stage, technical chargebacks, Visa/Mastercard guidelines (in brief), and reason codes in relation to fraud chargebacks. nbsp; /li li Communication Skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication. ○ Listening Skills: Ability to understand, anticipate, and resolve queries arising from various stakeholders. /li li Attention to Detail and Accuracy: Excellent organizational and multitasking skills, with the ability to identify anomalies or suspicious behaviors. /li li Friendly and pleasant demeanor over the phone and email. /li li Bachelor's Degree. nbsp; /li /ul p strong Location: Bangalore /strong /p div class= content-conclusion div class= gmail_default span style= font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12pt; span id= m_2989597180337834284gmail-m_4972969247898306296gmail-docs-internal-guid-3a65a3c2-7fff-88ff-9e94-8ab11a050d04 Razorpay b

You'll treat cloud cost and capacity as one roadmap, choosing the architecture, data models, and tools that let service owners manage their usage and spending. /p h2 strong What you'll do /strong /h2 ul li Build data pipelines that turn Google Cloud billing exports and Cloud Monitoring telemetry into a clean, queryable picture of fleet usage and utilization in BigQuery. /li li Attribute shared cost and usage across Google Kubernetes Engine clusters to the teams and services that drive them, using foundations such as OpenCost and Google Kubernetes Engine cost allocation. /li li Develop capacity and demand tooling that profiles infrastructure needs by machine family and region to support reservation planning and prevent capacity shortages. /li li Ship internal applications that let engineers and budget owners see and act on their cloud footprint, replacing manual snapshots and spreadsheets with software. /li li Establish the data models, services, and engineering standards that future team members will extend, and help shape technical direction and hiring as we grow. /li li Partner with Finance, product teams, service owners, and infrastructure engineers to turn their needs into technical designs. /li li Use artificial intelligence in your daily engineering workflow to improve efficiency and outcomes, as we expect of all GitLab team members. /li /ul h2 strong What you'll bring /strong /h2 ul li A track record of designing and shipping production backend services that you've owned end to end, beyond operating existing systems. /li li Strong structured query language (SQL) skills with large datasets, experience building and maintaining data pipelines and models, and comfort working with cloud billing and usage data. /li li Working knowledge of a major cloud platform, preferably Google Cloud, including compute services, Kubernetes, and pricing and billing models. /li li Proficiency in a general-purpose programming language for tooling and pipelines. We value your ability to build and ship over mastery of a single language; Go and Python suit this work, and we use Ruby across our product code. /li li The ability to break a new problem into milestones and drive it to production with light direction, communicating clearly in a remote, asynchronous environment. /li li Helpful, not required: OpenCost, Kubecost, or Google Kubernetes Engine cost allocation; cloud financial management (FinOps) practices or certification; cost or capacity modeling, forecasting, or anomaly detection; Terraform; Looker, Looker Studio, or Grafana; founding engineering work; or artificial intelligence in engineering workflows. /li /ul h2 strong About the team /strong /h2 p We're part of the Cloud Cost Utilization team within Infrastructure Platforms, working with Fleet Management. We partner with Finance, product teams, service owners, and infrastructure engineers as our service-ownership model matures.
